verified: planner_verdict_was_persisted() scans sorted events.jsonl* pathnames, prefilters lines by delivery_id text, skips JSONDecodeError lines, catches OSError around file scanning, and returns False after the scan when no verified matching event was found.

UnicodeDecodeError is not caught by planner_verdict_was_persisted(): the file is opened as UTF-8 and the outer exception handler catches OSError only. Thus invalid UTF-8 can escape this boolean persistence query rather than yielding a conservative unknown state.

A malformed JSON row that contains the target delivery_id is explicitly skipped on JSONDecodeError and can therefore contribute to a final False even though that damaged row cannot prove target absence.

The production retry authority in LifeSupervisor._retry_pending_planner_verdict() calls planner_verdict_was_persisted(); when it returns False, the supervisor is permitted to call _emit(event) again. This verifies the core false-absence-to-re-emission path at source level.

Repository code search at the pinned Argus commit surfaced the persistence helper definition and the supervisor core as the production-code locations for planner_verdict_was_persisted; tests reference the retry path separately.
Argus already declares portalocker>=3 and provides core.file_lock.exclusive_file_lock(), which uses portalocker.LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB with a bounded default timeout of 30 seconds.

The current event-log writer does not use that cross-platform helper: event_log.py conditionally imports fcntl and applies fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) only when fcntl is available. iter_call_events() enumerates event_log_paths() and opens those pathnames later, so it does not itself pin generation file handles under a stable snapshot.

Argus CI already includes tests/core/test_file_lock.py and tests/daemon/test_state_portable.py in the macOS/windows-latest portable matrix installed with .[qr], so a new portable event-lock regression can be attached to an existing real-Windows test surface.

At the pinned portalocker source, the platform documentation states that POSIX defaults to fcntl.flock; Windows defaults to the standard-library msvcrt path for exclusive locks; true shared locks on Windows require the optional win32/pywin32 extra.

material_scope_corrections.claim: The tri-state FOUND/ABSENT/UNKNOWN repair is already implemented and tested in Argus.
material_scope_corrections.correction: The pinned helper remains boolean. FOUND/ABSENT/UNKNOWN, stable-generation handle snapshots and the supervisor UNKNOWN short-circuit are proposed repairs, not current guarantees.

material_scope_corrections.claim: The current event writer already has cross-platform exclusion because Argus depends on portalocker.
material_scope_corrections.correction: The generic exclusive_file_lock helper is cross-platform, but the pinned JsonlEventSink writer still directly uses fcntl when available and takes no cross-process event lock on platforms where fcntl is absent. Dependency availability is not the same as adoption on this authority path.

material_scope_corrections.claim: A 30-second bounded portalocker helper can be reused unchanged without changing event-log semantics.
material_scope_corrections.correction: Current POSIX fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) is blocking with no application timeout in the event writer, while exclusive_file_lock defaults to 30 seconds. Reusing the helper unchanged could convert long contention into a write failure; the worker correctly leaves indefinite/event-specific policy as an implementation decision.

material_scope_corrections.claim: A production duplicate planner verdict has been observed.
material_scope_corrections.correction: This audit verifies a source-reachable false-absence/re-emission mechanism only. It does not estimate occurrence rate or establish a production incident.

tested_scope: pinned Argus source and pinned portalocker platform semantics; no full Argus runtime fault injection, Windows CI execution, or production incident evidence
downstream_note: The highest-confidence current defect is boolean absence authority under incomplete/corrupt scanning: unknown evidence can either raise or collapse to False, and False authorizes re-emission. Treat the typed tri-state and stable-snapshot lock changes as repair proposals until implemented and regression-tested.
